do: say it in the owner's plain words: no command, flag, exit code, file or field name, JSON; technical detail only inside a folded details.tech
example: The button never says --apply; the folded box "What exactly gets written" may list the fields.

do: read top down in one column: what waits first, grouped, one row per ask that opens in place; never a grid of cards holding tables
example: Ten asks are ten rows under four group headings; the first row is open, and a table sits inside its row.

do: the agent's suggestion is pre-selected and marked, and what "no" means (for a choice, what happens if none of the options fits) is stated, before any control
example: We suggest Yes and "If no: we keep calling them 50 g pouches" come first; the Yes radio is already checked. A choice says "If none fits:" there.

when: the answers are a fixed set
do: buttons, radios or a select, never a typed a|b; typing only for a provide ask, with its type and unit
example: Approve and Reject are two big radio rows; a cost is a number box with USD beside it.

do: a comment is optional; an empty one is fine
example: Add a comment (optional) is folded, and sending without opening it works.

do: it leaves the waiting page and is in History with what was shown, who, when, suggested or changed, and whether the agent has applied it, readable at a glance from the chip and the row's edge (amber waiting, green applied, plain and dimmed withdrawn); Reopen is offered only for an answer nothing has acted on, and one a system already took says so instead
example: Masala chai · Suggested · Waiting for the agent to apply, with a Reopen button until the agent applies it; an answer that was already written to a system has a line saying it cannot be taken back here.

do: the page says how many of the budget are used, and says so when over
example: 3 of 10 asks open beside ten small segments; over the limit the line turns red and says to answer some first.

do: the same top bar, current tab marked, language link; usable at 375 px with no sideways page scroll; tap targets ≥ 44 px
example: Under 480 px the tabs move to their own row; a wide table scrolls inside its own box.

do: the console's own words come only from the dictionary, both languages complete; the agent's words are shown as written
example: The Chinese page says "批准" on the button while the agent's English title stays as the agent wrote it.

do: a page nobody has touched (at the top, nothing typed, no row opened or closed) reloads by itself; any other stays as it is and a banner offers the reload; the count in the tab title follows every poll, hidden tab or not
example: While you type a comment and the agent posts a new ask, a bar says "This page has changed. Tap to reload." and your text stays; a page left alone at the top just reloads.

when: an answer writes to a harness
do: show what will be written before the button (for a choice, what each option would write), and after it what was written or the harness's own refusal
example: A folded "What exactly gets written" sits above the button, one row per option for a choice; the next page says "The system says: unit cost confirmed" or the system's reason for refusing.

do: only http(s), opens in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer"
example: A source link to https://example.com opens in a new tab; a javascript: address is shown as plain text, never as a link.

when: an ask approves something (spends, writes, sends)
do: it reads heavier than a confirmation: an amber edge on its row, what approving does in an amber box, an amber button while Approve is the picked answer; it is never answered as part of a group
example: The three bid changes sit in a Money group with no "Answer all" button, and their Approve button is amber where a confirmation's is blue.

when: an answer has to be written to a system this console cannot reach (no relay was set up, or its verb is not allowed here)
do: draw no form that would write it (a yes/no ask can still be declined, and that answer is marked as suggested only when the agent suggested it) and no group button that would include it; say in one plain sentence, before any click, that it has to be confirmed another way and to ask the agent
example: The unit-cost ask shows "This answer has to be confirmed another way. Ask the agent how." where its button would be.

when: an answer is on its way
do: it cannot go twice and nothing on the page can change or replace it: the buttons go dead after the first click, the page stops reloading and polling until the console has replied, and the mouse wheel over a number box never changes the number
example: A slow harness takes a minute: a second click does nothing, the page stays put, and when the reply comes the notice says what was written.

do: after three failed checks in a row a bar says so, what is typed stays, and the bar goes away by itself when the console answers again
example: Stop the console and about twelve seconds later a red bar says "Cannot reach the console right now. What you typed is still here."; start it again and the bar goes.

when: a form is sent (an answer, a group's answers, a note, a reopen, a view)
do: it is sent without leaving the page: what the console said shows over the page (a saved one goes by itself, a refusal stays until it is clicked away), then the rows are swapped for the current ones, keeping every row's open or closed state and everything typed but not sent; if the console cannot be reached the form comes back as it was; without script it is an ordinary form and a page of its own
example: Answer the third ask of ten: "Answer saved: Yes" appears at the top, the row leaves Waiting, the count in the tab goes from 10 to 9, and a comment half typed in the seventh row is still there. Reopen on History works the same way and stays on History.

when: someone may see the asks but not decide (an adviser, when the operator named who decides)
do: show them every ask and every answer and no control that answers, reopens or writes a note; each ask and answer offers Agree or Disagree with nothing picked, and a reason is required to disagree; the one who decides reads each view under its ask before the answer controls, the waiting page counts the disagreements, and an answer not yet applied that someone disagrees with opens in History with the reasons and Reopen at its top
example: Carol advises: the budget ask shows Agree and Disagree and a reason box where Alice sees the answer buttons. Carol disagrees with Alice's answer; Alice's waiting page says "Disagreements from the team: 1" and that History row opens with Reopen above the reasons.
